_comment: Version: 1 | Path: infra/c12_workflow/workflows/reembed_project.json | Description: D-011 R-400-229 re-embed trigger workflow. c8_admin POSTs this webhook with {job:'reembed', tenant_id, project_id, model_id} when a registry embedding model is edited (vectors change) or a project switches selection. n8n then calls C7 POST /projects/{project_id}/reembed AS THE SYSTEM (self-asserted project_owner headers, same convention as extract_and_ingest) — reembed is a CONTENT op and the triggering operator may be a content-blind platform_manager, so the recompute runs decoupled as the system, never under the operator identity. Re-embed ONLY (C7 recomputes vectors from the already-stored chunk text; no re-parse/chunk/LLM). onReceived → acks immediately, C7 reembed runs async. Import via `docker compose exec c12 n8n import:workflow --input=/workflows/reembed_project.json`. @relation implements:R-400-229
name: Re-embed Project (c8_admin -> C12 -> C7)

nodes.name: Webhook — POST /uploads/reembed-project
nodes.notes: Triggered by c8_admin (D-011 R-400-222). Body: { job: 'reembed', tenant_id, project_id, model_id }. Fire-and-forget best-effort — a failure is logged c8_admin-side and never blocks the admin op.

nodes.name: C7 POST /reembed
nodes.notes: System-authed reembed (self-asserted project_owner; NOT platform_manager, which is content-excluded). C7 recomputes vectors in place from stored chunk text — re-embed only. Long timeout: a large project re-embeds many chunks. The webhook already responded (onReceived); this runs async, so no respond node is needed.
